- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is trending up, model frequently underestimates the continuation; add 1–3% to forecast for next 3–7 days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in early 30d horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture volatility; use sentiment-weighted average of 0.5–0.7 to adjust forecast midpoint.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome is below 50% of 30d forecast range, model is overconfident; cap forecast at 95th percentile of historical 30d range for that sentiment cluster.
